definition: Subordinate means lower in rank or importance.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word subordinate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know subordinate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: In the kitchen brigade every station chef is subordinate to the executive chef, whose menu is law.
Junior is the gentlest step down — a junior partner merely arrived later and may still command plenty; subordinate states outright that another's authority stands above yours.
Menial sinks below subordinate: a subordinate officer still holds duties of judgment and trust, while menial work sits at the ladder's bottom — the tasks assigned when rank has run out entirely.

Secondary means second in importance — the side plot, the backup plan — whether or not any chain of command exists. Subordinate needs the chain: it places someone or something under another's formal authority. A secondary concern has no boss over it; a subordinate officer does.

Inferior says something is worse — lower in quality or worth, not merely in position. Subordinate is the org chart's word and carries no such insult: a subordinate officer may be the best soldier in the building and still rank below the colonel. Inferior judges; subordinate only locates.

Subordinate means lower in rank or importance.
The hospital's chart of command is printed inside every stairwell: residents are subordinate to attending physicians, who answer to the department chief.
A resident may disagree out loud — the good ones do — but once the attending decides, the resident carries it out.
Subordinate is the precise word for standing lower in a formal order: it does not call anyone less able or less valued, only lower-ranked — it is the org chart's word, not an insult.
Subordinate is the org chart's adjective: it states rank and nothing else — a subordinate role, a clause subordinate to the main sentence.
When contempt is wanted, this unit's noun underling supplies it; when only arrival order is meant, junior is kinder.
Note the noun use too: a manager's subordinates are simply those the chart places beneath her.

A film set looks chaotic until you learn who answers to whom.
Every department head -- camera, sound, costume -- is subordinate to the director, and each accepts that arrangement in writing before shooting begins.
The word carries no insult on a set.
The cinematographer may be the most decorated artist present and still defers on every creative call.
Crews are careful to keep the idea separate from talent or worth.
Authority runs through the chain so that a thousand small decisions land on one desk.
When a costume designer once ignored the chain and reshot a scene's wardrobe on her own, the studio's memo did not call her work bad.
